recipes.name: Oats Upma with Mixed Vegetables
recipes.health_benefit: Oats are rich in soluble fiber (beta-glucan), which can help reduce LDL cholesterol. Vegetables add essential vitamins, minerals, and additional fiber.
instructions: Dry roast oats in a pan for 2-3 minutes until lightly fragrant. Set aside.
Heat mustard oil in the same pan. Add mustard seeds and let them splutter. Add curry leaves, chopped onion, green chili, and grated ginger. Sauté until onion turns translucent.
Add mixed vegetables and cook for 3-5 minutes until slightly tender.
Add turmeric powder and salt, mix well.
Pour in water and bring to a boil. Reduce heat, add roasted oats, mix well and cover.
Cook for 5-7 minutes until oats absorb water and are cooked through.
Turn off heat, stir in lemon juice, and serve hot.

recipes.name: Grilled Fish with Palak Sabzi
recipes.health_benefit: Lean fish, especially fatty fish like salmon or mackerel (if available), provides Omega-3 fatty acids that are beneficial for heart health and may help manage triglycerides. Spinach is rich in fiber, antioxidants, and various micronutrients.
instructions: Marinate fish fillets with 1/2 tsp ginger-garlic paste, 1/4 tsp turmeric, 1/4 tsp red chili powder, salt, and lemon juice. Set aside for 15 minutes.
Heat 1 tsp mustard oil in a pan. Grill or pan-fry fish fillets for 3-4 minutes per side until cooked through. Set aside.
In another pan, heat 1 tsp mustard oil. Add chopped onion and sauté until golden.
Add remaining ginger-garlic paste, cumin powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, and red chili powder. Sauté for a minute.
Add tomato puree and cook until oil separates.
Add chopped spinach, salt, and cover. Cook until spinach wilts and releases its water (about 5-7 minutes).
Add garam masala and mix well. Serve the palak sabzi with grilled fish.

recipes.name: Lean Chicken & Vegetable Stir-fry
recipes.health_benefit: Provides lean protein from chicken and a wealth of vitamins, minerals, and fiber from assorted vegetables, supporting overall health and satiety without excessive saturated fat.
instructions: Heat oil in a large wok or pan over high heat.
Add chicken strips and stir-fry until browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.
Add onion, garlic, and ginger to the same pan. Stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add carrots and broccoli florets, stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until slightly tender-crisp.
Add bell peppers and cook for another 2 minutes.
Return chicken to the pan. Add soy sauce, vinegar, and black pepper. Toss everything to combine well.
Serve hot with a small portion of brown rice or quinoa.

recipes.name: Moong Dal Cheela with Mint Chutney
recipes.health_benefit: Moong dal is a lean source of plant-based protein and fiber, contributing to satiety and digestive health. It's a low-fat alternative to traditional fried breakfasts.
instructions: Drain soaked moong dal. Blend it with ginger, green chilies, cumin seeds, hing, and a little water to make a smooth batter. Adjust consistency to be like pancake batter. Add salt.
For chutney: Blend mint leaves, coriander leaves, green chili, and lemon juice with a little water until smooth. Add salt to taste.
Heat a non-stick tawa (griddle) and lightly grease it with 1/2 tsp mustard oil.
Pour a ladleful of batter onto the tawa and spread it into a thin circle.
Cook until the edges start to crisp and the top looks cooked. Flip and cook the other side until golden brown.
Repeat for remaining batter. Serve hot with mint chutney.

recipes.name: Fiber-Rich Vegetable Pulao with Tandoori Chicken
recipes.health_benefit: Brown rice provides complex carbohydrates and fiber, supporting satiety and steady blood sugar. Vegetables add micronutrients and fiber. Lean tandoori chicken offers high-quality protein with minimal fat.

ingredients.item: Whole spices (bay leaf, cinnamon stick, cloves, green cardamom)

instructions: Wash and soak brown rice for 20 minutes, then drain.

For Tandoori Chicken: Mix yogurt, tandoori masala, ginger-garlic paste (1/2 tsp), salt, and lemon juice. Marinate chicken pieces for at least 30 minutes. Bake or grill until cooked through (approx. 20-25 mins at 200°C/400°F).
For Pulao: Heat mustard oil in a pot. Add whole spices and let them crackle. Add sliced onion and sauté until golden brown.
Add remaining ginger-garlic paste and sauté for a minute.
Add mixed vegetables, turmeric powder, and biryani masala (if using). Sauté for 3-4 minutes.
Add soaked brown rice and salt. Gently mix.
Pour in water, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 20-25 minutes until rice is cooked and water is absorbed.
Fluff the pulao gently with a fork. Serve hot with baked Tandoori Chicken.

recipes.name: Heart-Healthy Dal Makhani (Reduced Fat)
recipes.health_benefit: Black lentils (urad dal) are highly fibrous and provide plant-based protein, which can contribute to better cholesterol management. This recipe uses minimal fat compared to traditional versions.
instructions: Drain soaked urad dal and rajma. Pressure cook them with enough water (about 3 cups) and a pinch of salt until very soft (8-10 whistles).
Heat mustard oil in a heavy-bottomed pan. Add chopped onion and sauté until golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies. Sauté for a minute until aromatic.
Add tomato puree and cook until oil separates and the mixture thickens.
Stir in cumin powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, and salt. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add the cooked dal and rajma (with their cooking liquid) to the masala. Mix well. If too thick, add more hot water to adjust consistency.
Simmer on low heat for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, allowing flavors to meld. Mash some of the dal against the side of the pan for a creamy texture.
Stir in garam masala and optional low-fat milk/light cream. Cook for another 2-3 minutes.
Serve hot with whole wheat rotis or brown rice.

recipes.name: Fenugreek (Methi) Chicken Curry
recipes.health_benefit: Fenugreek is known for its potential to help manage blood lipid levels, including cholesterol. Lean chicken provides high-quality protein. This recipe uses minimal oil and fresh ingredients.
instructions: Marinate chicken with 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp red chili powder, and salt for 15-20 minutes.
Heat mustard oil in a pan. Add chopped onion and sauté until golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies. Sauté for a minute until aromatic.
Add tomato puree and cook until oil separates and the mixture thickens.
Stir in cumin powder, coriander powder, remaining turmeric, and red chili powder. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add marinated chicken pieces and sauté on medium-high heat for 5-7 minutes until chicken changes color.
Add chopped fenugreek leaves and mix well. Cook for 2-3 minutes.
Pour in water, bring to a simmer, cover, and cook on low heat for 15-20 minutes until chicken is tender and cooked through.
Stir in garam masala. Serve hot with brown rice or whole wheat roti.

recommended_supplements.name: Omega-3 Fish Oil (EPA+DHA)
recommended_supplements.reason: Omega-3 fatty acids, particularly EPA and DHA, may help reduce triglyceride levels and could offer modest benefits in managing LDL cholesterol.
recommended_supplements.precaution: It is advisable to choose a purified/pharmaceutical-grade product. If you are taking blood-thinning medications (anticoagulants), discuss this with your healthcare provider as Omega-3s may increase bleeding risk. Take with food to enhance absorption and minimize gastrointestinal upset.
recommended_supplements.when_to_take: With your largest meal of the day (e.g., lunch or dinner).
recommended_supplements.duration: Ongoing, or as advised by your healthcare provider. Re-evaluation of lipid profile after 8-12 weeks is often helpful.

recommended_supplements.name: Plant Sterols / Stanols
recommended_supplements.reason: Plant sterols and stanols are clinically shown to reduce the absorption of dietary and biliary cholesterol from the gut, potentially leading to a 5–15% reduction in LDL cholesterol.
recommended_supplements.precaution: It is best to take this supplement with meals to maximize its effectiveness. They may slightly reduce the absorption of fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K), so ensuring adequate intake of these vitamins through diet or a multivitamin may be beneficial.
recommended_supplements.when_to_take: With your main meals (e.g., 1g with lunch and 1g with dinner).
recommended_supplements.duration: Ongoing, or as advised by your healthcare provider. Lipid levels can be rechecked after 8-12 weeks.
